Description: explicit — CJK labels in a chosen font where layers set text-font
prompt: I'm on the latest MapLibre GL JS. My style has a glyphs URL, and every label layer sets `text-font` to `["Roboto Regular"]`. Chinese place names render in the browser's default sans-serif. I want them drawn in Noto Sans SC, which I can host as a font file, without changing how the Latin labels look. How do I set that up?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a **step-by-step recipe** that lets you keep the existing **Roboto Regular** glyph-PBFs for all Latin text, but draw every Chinese character with a **self-hosted Noto Sans SC** file. The trick is to use the **`font-faces`** property (or `map.setFontFaces()` at runtime) to *override* the font that is used for a specific Unicode range while leaving the rest of the font-stack untouched. --- ## 1. What actually happens right now | Layer | `text-font` | `glyphs` URL | What GL JS does for Chinese | |------|-------------|--------------|-----------------------------| | your label layers | `["Roboto Regular"]` | `https://my-tileserver/font/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf` | `glyphs` URL has no CJK ranges → GL JS falls back to the **local-ideograph** path → the browser picks its default `sans-serif` (usually Arial/Helvetica). | Because the style **does have a `glyphs` field**, GL JS will try to fetch a PBF for every range that the font-stack requests. For CJK there is no range on the server, so the request fails and GL JS falls back to the local-font renderer (TinySDF). That renderer uses the map option `localIdeographFontFamily` (default: `"sans-serif"`). > **Goal:** keep the Roboto glyph-PBFs for Latin, but tell the local-font renderer to use **Noto Sans SC** for the CJK ranges. --- ## 2. Two ways to point the local-font renderer at Noto Sans SC | Method | When to use it | What it does | |--------|----------------|--------------| | **A. `localIdeographFontFamily` map option** | You *only* use the default `text-font` (i.e. you never override it with a custom stack). | Sets the font family that the *default-text-font* layers use for ideographs. | | **B. `font-faces` entry with a `unicode-range`** | You have a custom `text-font` (like `"Roboto Regular"`), or you want the override to apply *only* to the CJK range while leaving the rest of the stack untouched. | Maps the **same `text-font` name** to a different font file **only for the specified Unicode ranges**. The rest of the characters continue to be drawn from the glyph-PBFs. | Because your layers **explicitly set** `text-font: ["Roboto Regular"]`, **Method B** is the one that works without changing the style’s `text-font` values. --- ## 3. Host the Noto Sans SC file 1. Download the OTF/TTF you want, e.g. `NotoSansSC-Regular.otf` from Google Fonts. 2. Put it on a server that can be reached from the browser (same origin as your map page, or CORS-enabled). *Example URL:* `https://example.com/fonts/NotoSansSC-Regular.otf` Make sure the server sends **CORS headers** (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` or your domain) because GL JS loads the file via XHR. --- ## 4. Add a `font-faces` entry that overrides only the CJK range ### 4.1. In the **style JSON** (static approach) ```json { "version": 8, "glyphs": "https://my-tileserver/font/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf", "font-faces": { "Roboto Regular": [ { "url": "https://example.com/fonts/NotoSansSC-Regular.otf", "unicode-range": [ "U+3000-30FF", // CJK Symbols & Punctuation, Hiragana, Katakana "U+4E00-9FFF", // CJK Unified Ideographs "U+3400-4DBF", // CJK Unified Ideographs Extension A "U+20000-2A6DF", // CJK Unified Ideographs Extension B "U+2A700-2B73F", // CJK Unified Ideographs Extension C "U+2B740-2B81F", // CJK Unified Ideographs Extension D "U+2B820-2CEAF", // CJK Unified Ideographs Extension E "U+2CEB0-2EBEF", // CJK Unified Ideographs Extension F "U+F900-FAFF", // CJK Compatibility Ideographs "U+FF00-FFEF" // Half-width & Full-width Forms ] } ] }, "layers": [ { "id": "place-labels", "type": "symbol", "source": "osm", "source-layer": "place", "layout": { "text-field": ["get", "name"], "text-font": ["Roboto Regular"], "text-size": 12 } } /* … other layers … */ ] } ``` **What this does** * For every character **outside** the listed Unicode ranges, GL JS still looks for a glyph PBF in the `glyphs` URL (so Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, etc. keep using the Roboto Regular PBFs you already have). * For characters **inside** those ranges (i.e. all Chinese, Japanese, Korean ideographs and punctuation), GL JS **ignores the glyph server** and draws the glyphs from the **local Noto Sans SC** file you supplied. ### 4.2. Compare the visual appearance with a known Noto Sans SC rendering (e.g. Google Fonts preview) – the glyph shapes should match. If you still see the generic `sans-serif` font, double-check: * The **URL** to the OTF is reachable and CORS-enabled. * The **Unicode ranges** cover the characters you are testing (you can temporarily broaden them to `U+4E00-9FFF` only to see a change). * The **`text-font` name** in the style exactly matches the key you used in `font-faces` (`"Roboto Regular"` – case-sensitive, spaces matter). --- ## 7.
